summary: NTCA supports E-Rate program but urges cost-effective use of resources in well-served areas. Proposes overbuilding safeguards to ensure special construction funds are not used when affordable options already exist. The comments argue against restricting special construction or dark fiber for E-Rate projects, citing cost inefficiencies and the need for cost-effective use of funds. The comments highlight the existing robust fiber networks in place and the lack of proper safeguards in the competitive bidding rules that prevent the use of these existing networks. NTCA-The Rural Broadband Association opposes restricting special construction or dark fiber for E-Rate funding, citing cost inefficiencies and overbuilding issues in rural areas. The comments propose limiting or sunsetting E-Rate to avoid waste and ensure funds are used appropriately. They argue that funding duplicative connections is not cost-effective and that funds should be used to support the most cost-effective options, such as leveraging existing High-Cost supported connections or addressing true unavailability of outside plant network assets. NTCA urges the Commission to require school and library consortia to invite bids from multiple vendors to avoid big selling, indicating opposition to sunsetting the program.
